findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic, so one code can be used more than once
findings.body: Login decrypts `user.backupCodes`, finds the matching index, nulls it, and writes the re-encrypted blob back. Nothing guards this read-modify-write: there is no transaction and no optimistic check against the previously read value. Two concurrent sign-in requests with the same backup code (or two different codes) can both pass the `indexOf` check. As a result a supposedly single-use code can grant multiple sessions, and one request's update can overwrite the other's, un-consuming a code that was already used. Make the consumption conditional, e.g. `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }` and fail if the count is 0, or run it in a serializable transaction.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive although the UI suggests uppercase
findings.body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString('hex')`) and compared with an exact `indexOf`. The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which invites uppercase entry, and mobile keyboards often auto-capitalize. A valid code typed in uppercase is rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`. The input is also not trimmed, so surrounding whitespace causes the same rejection. Normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` before comparing, both here and in `totp/disable.ts`.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in request body causes an unhandled 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string. A JSON body with a numeric or object `backupCode` throws a TypeError, which surfaces as an internal server error instead of a 400. Validate the type, e.g. with zod or a `typeof` check, before use.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable and leaves stale state
findings.body: After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called immediately. It now runs only when the user clicks the new Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Escape, overlay click, via `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent never learns about it, so the settings switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled. `resetState()` also never runs, so the modal reopens on the DisplayBackupCodes step with stale codes. Handle dismissal on this step the same way as Close, or call `onEnable` when entering the step.

findings.title: Error message tells users to generate backup codes in settings, but no such feature exists
findings.body: `missing_backup_codes` reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Codes are only created during initial 2FA setup, and this PR adds no regenerate option. Every user who enabled 2FA before this change has no codes and cannot follow the instruction except by disabling and re-enabling 2FA. Either add a regeneration flow or reword the message.

findings.title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hashes
findings.body: Backup codes are single-use bearer credentials that only ever need to be verified. They are stored via `symmetricEncrypt` with the global `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so anyone with database and key access can recover every user's valid codes. Storing per-code hashes (e.g. SHA-256 of the high-entropy code, or bcrypt) and comparing against those would limit the impact of a compromise.

findings.title: No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The e2e changes only click the download, copy and close buttons. There is no test that a backup code authenticates, that a used code is rejected on reuse, or that disable works with a backup code; the TODO acknowledges this. Separately, the first test now leaves the backup-codes dialog open and relies on an `isChecked()` assertion that is admitted (FIXME) to always pass, so it no longer verifies that enabling succeeded.
